key_findings.finding: The encoded transformation is reduction of an ethyl ester, CCOC(=O)–, to a primary hydroxymethyl group, –CH2OH, with the rest of the N-substituted cyclic amine scaffold retained. Database standardization decoded the reactant as CCOC(=O)C1CCN(Cc2ccccc2)CC1 and product as OCC1CCN(Cc2ccccc2)CC1.

A directly matching documented record uses aluminum hydride/lithium hydride components (represented as [Al+3], [H-], [Li+]) in diethyl ether and gives the primary alcohol OCC1CCN(Cc2ccccc2)CC1. This is consistent with LiAlH4 ester reduction; aqueous/ basic workup components appear in another closely matching record.

Chemically plausible alternatives are borane complexes (BH3·THF or BH3·SMe2), which commonly reduce esters to primary alcohols under milder conditions, and DIBAL-H, which can reduce esters to aldehydes at controlled low temperature and therefore requires excess reagent/warmer conditions or optimization for full alcohol reduction. The retrieved database records directly document LiAlH4-type reduction but do not provide a direct borane or DIBAL-H match for this exact substrate.
